submission.natural_language_explanation: The negative pole fires on a closed family of formal, Latin-derived process and planning words - 'consider / consideration / considering', 'research', 'study', 'explore', 'improve', 'seek', 'mitigate', 'feasible', 'sufficient', 'assessment', 'analysis', ' per capita', 'red tourism', and the fixed phrases 'Did you know' and 'not only ... but also' - and on the function words (' of', ' that') that continue those phrases, but only when the word sits in the hedged, deliberative frame of written expository prose: after a deontic or necessity marker (should, ought to, must, need to, have to, 'recommend that you', 'it is important to'), after 'worth', after source-introducing 'According to', or inside those fixed constructions. It stays silent on the same words as the plain finite predicate of a simple declarative ('we consider the options', 'I know the answer', 'we study / we explore the proposal'), when 'will' replaces a deontic modal, when a near-synonym outside the family is used ('should examine / assess / evaluate / review'), and in casual narrative text; its opposite pole instead fires on policy-action and goal vocabulary (phase out, eradicate, fight against, campaign, priority), and every top negative peak is in the same g+u- SwiGLU regime, so this is one job, not two.
